The main goal is to remove [deprecated](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32361) code (removed in C++26).

This PR employs Microsoft's modern [approach](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/design/globalizing/use-utf8-code-page) to handling UTF-8:
> Until recently, Windows has emphasized "Unicode" -W variants over -A APIs. However, recent releases have used the ANSI code page and -A APIs as a means to introduce UTF-8 support to apps. If the ANSI code page is configured for UTF-8, then -A APIs typically operate in UTF-8. This model has the benefit of supporting existing code built with -A APIs without any code changes.

body:
## Overview
This PR introduces the CollectiveChoice governance smart contract, a blockchain-based voting system that enables community members to propose, deliberate on, and enact collective decisions in a transparent and equitable manner.

## Features
- **Motion Submission**: Community members can propose new motions with detailed content and a specified deliberation timeframe
- **Transparent Voting**: Members can cast affirmative or negative ballots on active motions
- **Deliberation Management**: Motion originators can adjust deliberation windows to ensure adequate discussion time
- **Motion Lifecycle Controls**: Includes full support for withdrawing motions and ratifying passed proposals
- **Read-only Data Access**: Provides query functions to retrieve motion details and current status

## Implementation Details
The contract implements several key components:
- **Motion Registry**: Stores all motion details including content, deliberation period, vote tallies, and status
- **Ballot Registry**: Tracks member participation to prevent duplicate voting
- **Motion Sequence**: Maintains a unique identifier for each submitted motion
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive validation with specific error codes for each failure scenario

## Public Functions
- `introduce-motion`: Submits a new proposal for community consideration
- `adjust-deliberation-window`: Modifies the voting timeframe for an active motion
- `submit-ballot`: Casts a vote on an active motion
- `withdraw-motion`: Removes a motion from consideration (originator only)
- `ratify-motion`: Finalizes a passed motion after deliberation period ends
- `view-motion-details`: Read-only function to retrieve motion information

## Security Considerations
- **Access Controls**: Only motion originators can withdraw or modify their proposals
- **Temporal Constraints**: Enforces proper deliberation periods with block height validation
- **Anti-Manipulation**: Prevents duplicate voting and ensures proper motion state progression
- **Content Limits**: Restricts motion content to reasonable size to prevent blockchain bloat

  - Timestamp attribute filters extend numeric filters to recognize timestamp
    text representations supported by CDateTime.
  - Text attribute filters support exact match, wildcard match, and regular
    expression match.
  - FileId filters extend numeric filters to also accept text patterns.
    Numeric filters apply to the attribute value itself. Text filters join
    with a corresponding FileInformation meta event and apply the filter to
    the Path attribute.

Refactored command and operation class hierarchies to facilitate reuse of

### Short description:
This feature allows Namespace objects to be passed into the get function of NamespacedResources. Pod.get is an example which can directly accept a namespace avoiding confusion of where Namespace exists as a string.

### More details:
It's annoying to juggle between namespaces as strings and namespace objects. If the Namespace is passed into a function such as Pod.get it results in the field resolving to __repr__ which is the default behavior. 

### What this PR does / why we need it:
I think this fixes two things but the implementation is mostly a suggestion. 
- When str, format or print is called on a Namespace instance, it resolves to a human-readable string.
- When a namespace is passed into a getter function, the name is used rather than the repr.
